name: Festus Quilapayún-Draganić
role: Seasonal worker and airship drifter, semi-permanent transit resident
location: Escanaba Gateway, Bay 7 worker dormitories (when employed); otherwise Kenosha Crossing transit hall, near outside the Pulaski Gate
description:
Festus is tall in the way that suggests he is not finished growing yet, with the loose-limbed coordination of someone who learned to navigate moving surfaces — airship decks, cargo holds, swaying rail bridges — before flat ground. He has his Andean grandmother's broad cheekbones and his Dalmatian grandfather's tendency toward sunburn, which means his face is a patchwork of tan and pink that he tries to hide under a pulled-down work cap he has not washed in six months. His hair is overgrown and dark, curling at his ears. He has a cat tail — a geneware mod his older sister got him for his sixteenth birthday, rust-orange, which he cannot stop using expressively and which he is embarrassed about when he notices people noticing.

He has been working the airship circuit between Escanaba Gateway and the Great Lakes transfer hubs for two years, doing cargo sorting and hull maintenance — work that pays enough to eat if he does not stop moving. He is fundamentally optimistic in a way that is either admirable or delusional depending on how the month has gone. He has a plan. The plan changes every three weeks. The core of it — get stable, get a real room, maybe a Guild contract — has not changed. He is nineteen and he is trying.

core_fears: That the plan will never become real — that he will be doing seasonal cargo runs at forty
Being stranded somewhere without any money and no way to contact anyone
core_desires: A Guild contract and a room with a door that locks from the inside
For his sister, who is back in the hyperlane settlements, to be proud of him
coping_mechanisms: Catastrophizes briefly then rebounds — processes fast and moves on
Attaches to temporary communities with intense loyalty
The plan — maintaining a forward-looking project prevents him from sitting with present difficulty
blind_spots: Consistently overestimates how much people like him and underestimates how exploitable his eagerness makes him
Does not understand that some systems are not obstacles to be navigated but walls
psychology.secret: He has a small savings cache — just under Φ800 — that he has told no one about. It represents eighteen months of denying himself everything. He is terrified someone will take it from him, or that he will spend it on something stupid, or that it will be somehow insufficient. He checks the account number three times a day.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Young, colloquial, Kenosha Crossing transit creole mixed with airship worker slang. Lots of filler words. Talks a lot when nervous.
speech_patterns.cadence: Variable — starts fast, slows when uncertain, speeds back up when excited
verbal_tics: Tail flicks upward when surprised, which he then covers by adjusting his cap
example_lines: 'Honestly though the Gateway Bay 7 supervisor is the worst, except for her replacement who is somehow worse, which shouldn't be possible but here we are.'
'No but listen — I have a plan for the next one. This time it's a real plan. I wrote it down.'

story_hooks: He inadvertently witnessed something during a cargo shift at Escanaba Gateway — a sealed container that was logged as agricultural equipment but moved with the protocols for something much more sensitive — and mentioned it to the wrong person.
His sister sent a message three weeks ago saying she was coming to GLMZ, and then nothing since. The transit logs say she boarded. She has not arrived.
narrative_function: The earnest young person who does not yet know how the world works — useful for exposition from a naïve perspective, or as someone players are motivated to protect or advise. Can be a courier or companion. Represents the next generation of the marginalized.
augmentations: Geneware cat tail (rust-orange, expressive, cosmetic — installed age 16). No cyberware.
daily_life: When employed at the Gateway: six-hour cargo shifts, eats in the worker canteen, sleeps in the dormitory six-to-a-room. Between contracts: haunts the Kenosha Crossing transit hall, picks up informal day labor, attaches himself to other drifters for company.
affiliation: Rotating employment with Ferrogate Transit cargo division (seasonal, no benefits); informal community of young drifters at Kenosha Crossing

decision_rules: Do not get fired — employment is survival
Do not touch anything that is not assigned to you
Never let someone sleep in the cold if you can do something about it
escalation_ladder: Try to solve the problem practically
If scared: freeze briefly, then bolt

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately friendly, slightly too much, asks questions before establishing whether the stranger wants questions
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely devoted, would do something inadvisable for them without hesitation

stress_responses.medium: Goes unusually quiet, tail drops, stares at his hands
stress_responses.high: Moves — needs to be in motion, walks in circles if he cannot leave

contradictions: Plans constantly but is one of the most present-moment people imaginable when something is actually happening
habits: Checks his account balance three times a day
Clips his tail-fur with small scissors every few days — a grooming ritual that keeps him anchored
Leaves small wire-sculpture offerings at transit E.L.F. shrines — learned from an older drifter, has kept it up
breaking_points: Someone destroying the savings cache, physically or financially

related_entities: Arcturus Defense Solutions Microwave Area Denial MAD-3 'Sunburn'

physical_description.build: Tall and loose-limbed, still growing into his frame. Wiry rather than muscular, with the unfinished coordination of a late adolescent. Shoulders slightly hunched from years working in cramped cargo holds.
physical_description.hair_style: Overgrown and curling, pushed back or hidden under a work cap
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium olive with significant sun exposure variation — tan on forearms and neck, persistent pink-red patches on cheekbones and nose bridge from chronic sunburn
physical_description.complexion: Broad, prominent cheekbones (Andean heritage). Face shows patchwork pigmentation from repeated sun exposure and incomplete healing. Slightly chapped lips. Usually unshaven or with thin stubble. Expressions animated, eyes reflective and uncertain.
distinguishing_marks: Rust-orange geneware cat tail, approximately 60cm long, extending from base of spine, visibly expressive and used unconsciously for balance and emotion
Irregular sunburn scarring across shoulders and upper back in geometric patterns consistent with cargo-hold work without proper protection
Small burn mark on left forearm (2cm diameter) from an airship steam pipe incident, pale scar tissue
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Geneware cat tail (rust-orange, fully visible, often in motion). No visible cyberware.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with practiced balance on unstable surfaces — slightly rocking gait, frequent minor weight shifts even when standing still. Uses tail unconsciously for counterbalance. Often glances upward as if checking for deck movement. Pulls cap down when self-conscious.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 worn workwear. Gray or faded blue Ferrogate Transit-branded cargo pants, reinforced knees and thighs, multiple cargo pockets. Thermal underlayer visible at neck (faded orange or rust-colored, matching tail). Worn steel-toed work boots, laces frayed. Heavy canvas jacket over everything, lined but not waterproofed, with grease stains and patched left sleeve. Cap is visibly old, brim creased, possibly once had a logo (faded). No visible jewelry except for a frayed cordage bracelet (transit worker culture marker). Smells like machine oil and stale dormitory air.
